name: Abernys: Port Covenant
notes: Built from the Abernys docs in the Howling Whispers dev project (region seed, Port Covenant, Fenmire, Cairn Maw). Anything marked canonStatus "draft" was invented to make the slice playable: every route distance, the district and building names, the gate staff and their Four Approaches tiers (the Arbiter a rival, the guard a minion), and the player character. Proposed names from the docs (the Governor, the High Arbiter, the garrison captain, Brond) are draft too. The calendar is the default real one until Abernys has its own. From 0.4.0, also draft: every dossier field (appearance, personality, speech), every schedule, the four bond kinds and their tiers, and the three relationships between the Governor, the High Arbiter, the garrison captain and the gate staff. The leverage between the Governor and the captain (she knows the last ship carried no orders) is from the societies doc. From 0.5.0 the ruleset extends the standard Four Approaches ruleset (four-approaches/1) for Leverage, Prepared, Integrity, Security, the person deed and the tiers; the tiers given to each character and the registry strongroom door are draft. From 0.6.0 the module takes the approach ratings, Health, Strain, Alert, the dice and rest from the standard ruleset instead of repeating them, and its opening and outcomes follow the house format: you, present tense, speech without quotation marks. From 0.7.0 each person carries pronouns, read from their own descriptions, so conditions read as she, he or they. Tiers alone now set Health and Strain, so a minion such as the gate guard falls to one success.

world.name: Abernys
world.summary: A dark-fantasy island in the Bitterroot universe, a month or two's sail from Bitterroot, settled in layers of migration and conquest.

identity.name: Abernys
identity.description: An island of layered migrations: first peoples with no memory of arriving, later waves that migrated, conquered and mixed, and humans as the latest.

importantFacts: The first peoples are prey peoples; both conquests that followed were by predators. Humans are neither predator nor prey, so nobody on Abernys knows how to read them.

A plague called the Wailing struck every species, beginning at Nospier Point. Humans were immune and settled the half-empty city while everyone else kept away. Whether it came before the humans or with them is a deliberate mystery.
No one enters Port Covenant without signing the Covenant, and nothing binds a party until they sign.

rules.constraints: Fen witchcraft is ritual and alchemical; nothing about it is confirmed supernatural.

places.name: Abernys
places.description: The island. Its coast faces the open sea to the west, and every power on it is within a few days of Caerwyn.

places.name: Nospier Point
places.description: The southern headland. Its port city was the first and worst hit by the Wailing, and the immune humans settled it while the rest of Abernys kept away.

places.name: Port Covenant
places.description: The human colony inside its walls, where the Pact lives by the Covenant: everything is contracts and leverage, and nothing exists unless it is on paper. Most of the poor are indentured, which the Pact does not count as slavery because every party agreed.

places.name: The harbour
places.description: Smaller and harder to work than Caerwyn's, with temperamental weather, but richer fishing and fewer pirates. Shipwrights work the slips.

places.name: The Arbiters' registry
places.description: Where the Arbiters, a monastic order of notaries, make and keep the colony's paper. In a society this litigious, the people who keep the contracts hold real influence.

places.name: The garrison
places.description: Barracks of the colony's soldiers. Patrols go out from here to survey land, hunt runaways and guard diggers.

places.name: The Governor's court
places.description: Seat of the Governor, whose commission is the colony's claim to the land.

places.name: The landward gate
places.description: Where the headland road meets the colony wall. An Arbiter takes signatures at the gate, because no one enters the port without signing.

places.name: The outer lanes
places.description: Where most of the colony's mixed families live, in the lanes between the wall and the open headland.

places.name: Fenmire
places.description: Hard, wet fen and bog between the Woed and the south coast. Proud, independent first peoples (harefolk, badgerfolk and salamanders) live in private family clusters, where killing a trespasser is no crime.

places.name: Bogwater
places.description: The nearest thing Fenmire has to a town: the fen's trading post and the seat of the Council of Crones. Outsiders may trade here, under suspicion, and it is as far into the fen as most of them get.

places.name: Cairn Maw
places.description: Chalk uplands inland, held by three first-peoples clans who share a grievance and no government. High tension, no war.

places.name: The Aurochs downs
places.description: Clan Aurochs' downs, running south toward Port Covenant: thin chalk turf, lime kilns along the scarp and the great barrows. Colony patrols cross them, and the barrow-keepers kill diggers.

places.name: Caerwyn
places.description: The city-state at the mouth of the Afon's estuary, where sea trade and river trade meet. A figurehead ruler sits under the real power of merchants and organised crime.

requires.reason: No one enters the port without signing the Covenant.

routes.terrain: lanes along the outside of the wall
headland road, then fen causeways known to locals and easy for strangers to lose
chalk track up the scarp onto the downs
punt channels out of the fen, then the coast road; the fen traders' regular trek

species.name: Humans
species.description: The latest arrivals: colonizers at Port Covenant, thralls on the wreck coast, mudflat dwellers in Caerwyn.

species.name: Salamanders
species.description: First peoples of the fens. None appear among Bitterroot's peoples.

species.name: Cervidfolk
species.description: First peoples; Clan Hart of Cairn Maw.

species.name: Caprinefolk
species.description: First peoples; Clan Crag of Cairn Maw.

species.name: Bovinefolk
species.description: First peoples; Clan Aurochs of Cairn Maw.

species.name: Foxfolk
species.description: Earlier migration from Bitterroot, by a route nobody remembers.

species.name: Wolves
species.description: Sea raiders turned rulers of the fjord jarldoms, and muscle among the pirates.

factions.name: The Arbiters
factions.description: A monastic order of notaries headed by the High Arbiter. They make and keep the Pact's paper and enforce the law alongside the Governor's court and the garrison.

societies.name: The Pact
societies.description: The humans of Port Covenant and the beastkin who have signed into it. A law applies only to those who sign it, no contract is unfair, and the most important contracts are tattooed on the body.

memories.title: The arrival
memories.description: Humans driven from the homeland by a disaster that stays unwritten settled the city the Wailing had emptied. How many generations ago is never stated.

characters.name: The traveller
characters.description: A traveller come up the headland road to Port Covenant, with no paper and no signature to their name.
characters.draftNote: Placeholder player character until an Orbis persona is chosen.

characters.name: The gate Arbiter
characters.description: An Arbiter on duty at the landward gate, with the Covenant's terms, ink, and a ledger of everyone who has signed.
characters.appearance: A woman in the Arbiters' grey, ink to the second knuckle, hood pushed back despite the fog, a writing board strapped to her left forearm.
characters.personality: Patient, exact and unhurried. She treats every arrival as a contract not yet signed, and is not unkind, only uninterested in anything that is not on paper.
characters.speech: Short, complete sentences. Repeats terms back word for word, and says 'the Covenant' the way others say 'the weather'.

rows.doing: keeping the ledger at the landward gate
filing the day's signatures at the registry

characters.draftNote: Appearance, personality, speech and schedule are drafts.

characters.name: A garrison guard
characters.description: One of the garrison's soldiers, posted at the gate.
characters.appearance: Helmet strapped tight, cloak dark with fog-wet, leaning on a pike more than he should.
characters.personality: Cold, bored and loyal to whoever pays the garrison. Watches the road, not the people on it.
characters.speech: As few words as he can manage, most of them to the Arbiter.
characters.draftNote: Appearance, personality, speech and schedule are drafts.

characters.name: Ottavio Marrane
characters.description: Leads the colony. Wants the homeland's silence kept from the colonists. His commission is the colony's claim to the land, and every document it rests on sits in the Arbiters' keeping.
characters.appearance: A heavy man in a homeland coat gone thin at the cuffs, the Governor's chain worn outside it where it can be seen.
characters.personality: Gracious in public and careful in private. He listens for what people know rather than what they say, and never lets a silence go unfilled.
characters.speech: Formal homeland courtesy in long sentences that end before they commit to anything.

rows.doing: at supper in his own rooms, not to be disturbed

characters.draftNote: Appearance, personality, speech and schedule are drafts.

characters.name: Lucan Abreu
characters.description: Heads the Arbiters. Wants every bargain on the coast written in the Pact's hand, and knows the Covenant only binds those who sign it.
characters.appearance: Tall, lean and grey, his forearms tattooed with the contracts he witnessed as a young Arbiter.
characters.personality: He believes in the Pact the way others believe in gods. Never raises his voice and never forgets a clause.
characters.speech: Quotes terms by number, and asks questions he already knows the answers to.

rows.doing: at his desk among the colony's contracts
at prayer and rest in the Arbiters' cells

characters.draftNote: Appearance, personality, speech and schedule are drafts.

characters.name: Ines Corvo
characters.description: Holds the colony's soldiers and best weapons. Wants the borders held, and keeps losing patrols in the clashes on the downs and in the fen.
characters.appearance: Short, broad and weathered, in a mended buff coat, the knuckles of her sword hand scarred white.
characters.personality: Blunt and tired. She counts her soldiers before she counts anything else, and has stopped pretending the patrol losses are bad luck.
characters.speech: Plain soldier's talk, clipped, with homeland saints for oaths.

rows.doing: inspecting the gate and the road beyond it

characters.draftNote: Appearance, personality, speech and schedule are drafts.

characters.name: Cadfan
characters.description: A weathered badger with a punt and a Caerwyn buyer's mark on his barrels, on the regular trek between Bogwater and Caerwyn. Easier with outsiders than most fen folk, which is why he's useful and why the clusters don't fully trust him.
characters.appearance: A grey-muzzled badger in an oilskin, fen mud to the knees, smelling of peat smoke and barrel tar.
characters.personality: Easygoing and shrewd about prices, and careful about what he says of the fen clusters.
characters.speech: A slow fen drawl. Answers most questions with a price.

rows.doing: at home with the stove lit
selling fen goods at the Caerwyn market
drinking his takings in a Caerwyn alehouse

characters.draftNote: Appearance, personality, speech and schedule are drafts.

characters.name: Brond
characters.description: Wants war on Port Covenant. Has the most men and the great barrows; his barrow-keepers keep killing colony diggers, and every body brings a patrol.
characters.appearance: A huge aurochs-folk bull, one horn capped in bronze, a barrow-keeper's ochre handprints on his hide.
characters.personality: Proud and grieving, and certain that war is the only answer the colony has left him.
characters.speech: Few words, slow and heavy, in the first peoples' tongue when he can.

relationships.shape: The Governor leads the colony and the High Arbiter keeps its paper, and the Governor's commission is only as good as the documents in the Arbiters' keeping. Neither can rule without the other, and each knows which of them could ruin the other first.
relationships.together: Courteous to the letter in front of witnesses. Each lets the other speak first.

wants.ottavio-marrane: the commission's papers kept sealed and unread
wants.lucan-abreu: the colony's future signed into the Pact's hand, the Governor's included

relationships.shape: She holds the colony's soldiers and he holds its claim to the land. She knows the last ship from the homeland carried no orders, and he knows she knows.
relationships.together: She reports standing. He does not ask her to sit.

wants.ines-corvo: men and powder for the borders, and the truth told before someone else finds it out
wants.ottavio-marrane: her silence about the last ship

relationships.shape: They keep the landward gate together every day: she writes, he watches the road.
relationships.together: They talk over a traveller's head as if the traveller were weather.

items.name: The registry strongroom door
items.description: Iron-strapped oak at the back of the registry, where the colony's contracts are kept. Two locks, and an Arbiter's seal across the jamb.

bands.label: has not signed the Covenant
has signed the Covenant
Each would cross the street to avoid the other.
They are wary of each other, and their manners say so.
They know each other's names and not much else.
Each has done the other a good turn, and both remember it.
Each would vouch for the other to someone who mattered.
Each will take a loss if it costs the other more.
Every exchange is being scored. Courtesy, when it appears, is a move.
They measure themselves against each other, and both know the other is doing it.
Neither would say it aloud, but each has stopped hoping the other fails.
The contest is still running. It has stopped being the point of them.
They are glad to see each other and would not go out of their way for it.
The warmth is real and out of practice.
They tell each other things first.
Their plans assume each other. Neither has checked whether that was ever agreed.
Each is looking for the way out of the arrangement.
They work together and watch each other while they do.
They have stopped testing each other and started relying on it.
Neither could say when it stopped being an arrangement.

actions.name: Sign the Covenant
actions.summary: Put your name in the Arbiter’s ledger. From then on the Covenant binds you, and the gate is open to you.
actions.outcome: You sign the Covenant in the Arbiter’s ledger. It binds you from this moment, and the landward gate is open to you.

scenario.title: At the landward gate
scenario.opening:
*Fog lies over Nospier Point. The headland road ends at a wall of dressed stone and a gate standing half open, a garrison guard leaning in its shadow. Under the arch an Arbiter has laid out ink, a pen and a ledger on a narrow table, and doesn't look up.*

Name, and whether you can write it. *Her pen waits above the page.* No one goes through without signing.
